llm.summary: This skill appears intended to generate Harness project documentation, but it can overwrite repository policy, CI, and test files without clear safeguards.

dimensions.detail: The script operates on the current repository and creates or replaces files under docs, AGENTS.md, .github/workflows, scripts, and Java test paths, which is high impact for a documentation-oriented helper without containment or overwrite checks.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time execution, external dependency installation, network retrieval, or privilege escalation mechanism was found. The package contains a Node script intended to be run manually.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documented --init flow generates all outputs, including .github/workflows/harness-ci.yml and src/test Java test code, with no dry run, confirmation, force flag, or per-file opt-in.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No system persistence or credential handling was found, but generated AGENTS.md and GitHub Actions workflow files persist in the repository and can affect future agent behavior and CI execution if committed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose mostly matches the artifact: SKILL.md discloses AGENTS.md, architecture docs, quality grades, GitHub Actions CI, and Java ArchUnit test generation. The capability is broader than passive documentation but not hidden.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the generated changes before committing. Do not run --init in an established repository unless you are willing to replace AGENTS.md, docs, CI workflow files, and possibly Java test files; prefer running it in a clean branch and checking the diff carefully.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded from a purpose-mismatch claim: SKILL.md does disclose CI configuration and architecture-test generation, though the high-impact nature is not strongly called out.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-only presentation is apparent from the artifact and is not a material security concern by itself.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted in part: file creation is disclosed, but overwrite behavior and the implications of repository policy, CI, and test-file changes are under-controlled.
[SDI-1] expected: Accepted as a Review concern: the generated workflow and test code are disclosed but expand the skill into executable repository artifacts.
[SDI-2] expected: Accepted for CI workflow generation: writing .github/workflows/harness-ci.yml is purpose-related but high impact when bundled into --init without confirmation or overwrite protection.
[SDI-2] expected: Accepted for Java architecture-test generation: the code is not malicious, but adding executable test source can affect builds and should be separately controlled.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as the central material concern: fs.writeFileSync is used on AGENTS.md, documentation, workflow, and test destinations without preserving existing files or requiring explicit replacement approval.
